attrs.title: Signs you need a proper account setup
attrs.lead: Most new accounts lose money in the first month for the same few reasons. If any of these sound like you, a proper setup usually pays for itself.

items.title: You’re about to run Google Ads for the first time
items.text:
Google makes it easy to start: a few clicks and your ads are live. The default settings, though, are built to spend, not to find customers. Broad keywords, Display placements and automatic bidding all switch on unless you turn them off.

We set the account up the way a specialist would run it: tracking first, then tight keywords, negative lists, campaigns by service and ads that match the search. Your first budget then buys useful data, not random clicks.

items.title: Your first attempt cost money and brought nothing
items.text:
Many companies try Google Ads once, spend a few thousand and decide it doesn’t work. Usually the problem isn’t Google Ads: the account had no tracking, showed on Display and paid for searches that were never going to buy.

We look at what happened in the first attempt, keep what worked and rebuild the rest. You get a clean account with tracking tested, so this time you can see what each click brings.

items.title: You started with a Smart campaign
items.text:
Smart campaigns, and accounts set up over the phone with Google, are quick to launch but give you little control. You can’t choose match types, you see few search terms and results are often counted as map clicks rather than enquiries.

We move you to standard Search campaigns with keywords you choose, proper conversion tracking and full search term reports. You keep the history and gain the control.

items.title: You’re launching a new product, service or country
items.text:
A new market has its own searches, competitors, languages and costs. Adding it to an existing campaign mixes the results, so the new market either starves or takes budget from what already works.

We research the new market, build its own campaigns with its own budget and landing pages, and set the locations and languages correctly. You see clearly how the launch is doing.

items.title: You want to run it yourself, after a good start
items.text:
Plenty of companies can manage a small account in-house once it’s built well. What they don’t have is the time or experience to set up the structure, tracking and negatives properly the first time.

We build the account, then hand it over with an account map, a weekly checklist and a training call. For 30 days after launch you can ask us anything.

items.title: Your account was set up by someone you can’t reach
items.text:
We often meet companies whose account, Tag Manager or Analytics was created by a freelancer or a former employee. Billing, admin access and the tracking all sit with someone who has moved on.

We make sure you own everything: the Google Ads account, billing, Tag Manager and GA4, with admin access in your name. Then we set it up properly from there.

attrs.label: How we set it up
attrs.html:
How we set it up

About two weeks from brief to launch. You approve the plan and see every campaign before anything goes live.

  1. A call to understand what you sell, who buys it, where they are and what a customer is worth to you. We also check what you already have: an old account, Analytics, Tag Manager, your website and any past results.

    You get: A one-page brief we agree on together.

    • What you sell and to whom
    • Which services or products matter most
    • Locations, languages and opening hours
    • What a lead or sale is worth

  2. We research the keywords people use to find what you sell, what they cost and who else is bidding. We look at competitors’ ads and landing pages, and we list the searches you should never pay for.

    You get: A keyword plan and a budget you approve.

    • Keywords with volumes and costs
    • Competitors’ ads and offers
    • Negative keyword lists
    • A budget estimate from real costs

  3. Tracking comes before any campaign. We set up conversion actions for calls, forms and sales, link GA4 and Tag Manager, and test each one with real submissions and calls.

    You get: A tracking sheet showing each test.

    • Forms, calls and sales tracked
    • Enhanced conversions where possible
    • GA4 and Tag Manager linked
    • Every conversion tested

  4. We build the campaigns, ad groups, keywords and ads by hand, set locations, schedules and networks, and add every asset. If a landing page is weak, we tell you what to change before launch.

    You get: Every campaign ready, for you to review.

    • Campaigns by service or product
    • Ads and assets for each ad group
    • Locations, schedule and networks set
    • Landing page notes

  5. We launch with a sensible budget, check search terms in the first days and add negatives as they appear. You get a training call, an account map and a checklist, and 30 days to ask us anything.

    You get: A live account, and the know-how to run it.

    • Search terms checked in week one
    • Negatives added as needed
    • A one-hour training call
    • Answers for 30 days

What we set up

Eight parts of a new account, set up before launch

For each part: why it matters, what we set up, the mistakes we see in new accounts and what you get.

Area 1 of 8

Account, billing and access

The account should belong to you. Many companies find later that a freelancer or former employee holds the only admin login, or that billing sits on someone’s personal card.

What we set up

  • Account created or recovered in your name
  • Billing and invoices in your company name
  • Admin access for you, standard for us
  • Manager account link you can remove
  • Time zone and currency
  • Auto-tagging on

Mistakes we see

  • ! Admin access held by a freelancer
  • ! Billing on a personal card
  • ! Wrong time zone, so reports never match
  • ! Auto-tagging off, so GA4 can’t see the clicks

What you get

  • An account you fully own
  • Clean billing and invoices
  • Access you control, and can take away from us
  • Settings that won’t need fixing later

Area 2 of 8

Conversion tracking

Tracking tells Google which clicks became customers. Without it you can’t see what works, and smart bidding has nothing to learn from.

What we set up

  • Form submissions
  • Calls from ads and from the website
  • Purchases with their value
  • Enhanced conversions
  • Primary and secondary goals
  • A test of every action

Mistakes we see

  • ! No tracking at all
  • ! Page views counted as conversions
  • ! Calls not tracked, though most leads phone
  • ! The same lead counted twice

What you get

  • Every real enquiry and sale tracked
  • Calls tracked with call reporting
  • Only real results as primary goals
  • A tracking sheet with each test

Area 3 of 8

Keyword research

Keywords decide which searches you pay for. The right list is specific, matched to what you sell and checked against what each click costs.

What we set up

  • Keywords by service or product
  • Search volumes and costs
  • Buying searches vs research searches
  • Match types
  • Competitor and brand terms
  • Local and language variations

Mistakes we see

  • ! A handful of broad, expensive keywords
  • ! Broad match with no negatives
  • ! Keywords for things you don’t sell
  • ! No local variations for a local business

What you get

  • A keyword plan by campaign
  • Phrase and exact match to start
  • Costs and volumes for each group
  • A shortlist to test later

Area 4 of 8

Campaign structure

Structure decides how budget is shared and which ad shows for which search. A clear structure is easy to read, easy to manage and easy to grow.

What we set up

  • Campaigns by service, product or location
  • Ad groups by theme
  • Budget per campaign
  • A separate brand campaign
  • Naming that anyone can follow
  • Room to grow

Mistakes we see

  • ! One campaign with every keyword
  • ! One ad group with 200 keywords
  • ! Brand and non-brand mixed
  • ! Budget going to the cheapest service, not the best

What you get

  • A campaign for each thing you sell
  • Tight ad groups with matching ads
  • Budgets set by what each service is worth
  • An account map you can follow

Area 5 of 8

Ads and assets

The ad is what people see. It should repeat their search, say why you, and give a clear next step. Assets add calls, links and prices that make the ad bigger.

What we set up

  • Responsive search ads per ad group
  • Headlines that match the search
  • Sitelinks, callouts and snippets
  • Call and location assets
  • Images and logo
  • Landing page for each ad group

Mistakes we see

  • ! One ad for every keyword
  • ! Headlines copied from the homepage
  • ! No assets, so the ads are small
  • ! Every ad sending people to the homepage

What you get

  • Ads written for each ad group
  • All relevant assets added
  • Calls and locations shown in the ad
  • A page for each service, or notes on what to build

Area 6 of 8

Negative keywords

Negative keywords stop you paying for searches that will never buy, such as jobs, free, DIY or courses. They matter most in the first weeks.

What we set up

  • Account-level negative lists
  • Jobs, free, DIY and training searches
  • Competitor names you don’t want
  • Locations you don’t serve
  • Cross-campaign negatives
  • A weekly search term check

Mistakes we see

  • ! No negatives at all
  • ! Paying for “jobs” and “salary” searches
  • ! Two campaigns bidding on the same searches
  • ! Search terms never checked

What you get

  • Negative lists in place before launch
  • Clean separation between campaigns
  • Search terms checked in week one
  • A checklist to keep doing it

Area 7 of 8

Locations, networks and schedule

A few settings, left on their defaults, quietly send budget to the wrong places: people outside your area, Display placements and searches in the middle of the night.

What we set up

  • Locations by presence, not interest
  • Display and search partners off
  • Ad schedule for your opening hours
  • Languages
  • Devices
  • Location exclusions

Mistakes we see

  • ! Ads shown to people “interested in” your city from abroad
  • ! Display Network on in a Search campaign
  • ! Ads running when nobody can answer the phone
  • ! Wrong language settings

What you get

  • Locations set to people in your area
  • Search only until there’s data
  • Ads timed to when you can respond
  • Settings checked on every campaign

Area 8 of 8

Budget and bidding

A new account has no data, so automatic bidding has nothing to learn from yet. The budget should be big enough to learn, and the bidding should match the stage you’re at.

What we set up

  • Daily budgets per campaign
  • A starting bid strategy
  • When to move to smart bidding
  • Cost-per-click limits
  • Budget forecast from real costs
  • A plan for the first 90 days

Mistakes we see

  • ! A target cost per lead set on day one with no data
  • ! A budget too small for even five clicks a day
  • ! All budget going to one campaign
  • ! No plan for when to change bidding

What you get

  • A budget that buys enough clicks to learn
  • Manual or maximise clicks with limits to start
  • Smart bidding once conversions come in
  • A 90-day plan

attrs.title: Why new accounts waste money
attrs.lead: The mistakes we see most in new accounts, what they look like in the first weeks, and how we set it up instead.

items.title: Broad match with no negatives
items.problem: Broad keywords with no negative lists pay for jobs, free and DIY searches from the first day.
items.fix: Phrase and exact match to start, with negative lists built before launch.

items.title: Display on in a Search campaign
items.problem: New Search campaigns include Display by default, so budget goes to apps and websites.
items.fix: Search only at launch; Display tested later, in its own campaign.

items.title: No conversion tracking
items.problem: Without tracking you can’t tell which keywords bring customers, and Google can’t either.
items.fix: Calls, forms and sales tracked and tested before the first click.

items.title: Ads shown far from your area
items.problem: The default location option includes people only “interested in” your area, wherever they are.
items.fix: Locations set to people in or regularly in your area, with exclusions.

items.title: Smart bidding with no data
items.problem: A target cost per lead on day one leaves Google guessing, so it either overspends or barely spends.
items.fix: Simple bidding with limits first, then smart bidding once conversions come in.

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
Google Ads Account Setup questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: How do I set up a Google Ads account?
items.answer: Create the account, set billing, add conversion tracking, research keywords, build campaigns and ads, then launch with a small budget and review search terms weekly.

items.question: How much should I spend on Google Ads to start?
items.answer: Enough to get meaningful data, usually enough for at least 50 to 100 clicks a week on your main campaign. We estimate it from real costs in your market.

items.question: How long does a Google Ads setup take?
items.answer: About two weeks from the brief to launch. Larger accounts or new markets can take three.

items.question: Can I run the account myself after setup?
items.answer: Yes. You get an account map, a weekly checklist, a training call and 30 days of questions. Or we can manage it for you.

items.question: Will I own the account?
items.answer: Yes. The account, billing, Tag Manager and Analytics are in your name. We only ever have access you can remove.

items.question: Do you set up Performance Max too?
items.answer: Usually we start with Search, where you have the most control. Performance Max comes later, once tracking and data are in place.
